text.en: A brick wall is made of bricks, and the body is made of cells. Groups of similar cells doing one job together make a tissue.

A tissue is a group of similar cells that together perform a particular function.
Plant tissues are meristematic (cells that keep dividing, at the tips of roots and shoots) and permanent (cells that have taken a fixed shape and job).
Simple permanent tissues: parenchyma (storage), collenchyma (flexibility) and sclerenchyma (strength).
Complex permanent tissues: xylem carries water and minerals up; phloem carries food from the leaves to other parts.
Animal tissues are epithelial (covering and lining), connective (blood, bone, cartilage), muscular (movement) and nervous (messages).
Muscles may be striated (skeletal, voluntary), smooth (involuntary, in organs) or cardiac (heart, involuntary).
Several tissues together form an organ and organs working together form an organ system.

problem.en: Which plant tissue carries water, and which carries food?

text.en: Water and minerals from the roots travel upwards in the xylem.
Food made in the leaves moves to the rest of the plant through the phloem.

why.en: Phloem carries sugars both up and down.

text.en: So xylem carries water and phloem carries food.

prompt.en: Name the main plant and animal tissues and their jobs.

points.en: Tissue = group of similar cells with one function.
Meristem divides; permanent tissues have fixed jobs.
Animal tissues: epithelial, connective, muscle, nervous.
